description: Single source of truth for dependency-update risk tiers. Consumed by the GitHub auto-merge workflow, the Azure DevOps PR policy script, and the config generator.

cooldown.comment: Wait this many days after a release before proposing it, so we do not adopt a version that gets yanked. Supported natively by GitHub Dependabot; enforced by Set-DependabotPrPolicy.ps1 on Azure DevOps.

comment: GLOBAL KILL SWITCH for automatic merging.
enabled: false  (current)
Dependabot opens pull requests and stops there. Nothing merges without a
person clicking merge. The policy engine still runs: it classifies every
PR, applies labels, and posts the rationale as a comment - so a reviewer
can see at a glance that a PR is a major bump of a pinned package rather
than a routine patch. It simply never calls 'gh pr merge --auto' on
GitHub, and never sets auto-complete or casts an approval vote on
Azure DevOps.
enabled: true
The per-tier 'autoMerge' flags below take effect and low-risk updates
merge themselves once the required checks pass.
The per-tier flags are deliberately left intact while this is false. They
document the intended risk model, and flipping this one boolean turns it on
without re-deriving which tiers were supposed to be automatic.
HOW DEPENDABOT CHOOSES A TARGET VERSION - read this before changing anything below.
1. VERSION UPDATES go to the LATEST release permitted by the manifest constraint.
2. SECURITY UPDATES go to the MINIMUM release that fixes the advisory, not the latest.
3. 'versioningStrategy' decides whether the DECLARED constraint is rewritten or only
the lockfile is refreshed. This is the main lever for 'stop changing my csproj'.
auto                  - ecosystem default.
increase              - always raise the declared requirement (^1.2.0 -> ^2.0.0).
increase-if-necessary - only raise the declared requirement when the new version
falls outside the existing range. Preserves intentional ranges.
lockfile-only         - never edit the manifest. Only refresh the resolved version
in the lockfile. Strongest 'my declared versions are law' mode.
Supported for npm/yarn/pnpm, pip, bundler, composer, cargo.
NOT supported for nuget - NuGet has no separate lockfile by
default, so pinning there is done via the manifest + pins below.
widen                 - widen the accepted range instead of moving it (npm, composer).
THE PINNING MODEL. Two modes, and picking the right one matters.
mode: 'soft'  (DEFAULT, and what you should reach for first)
Dependabot STILL OPENS THE PR. The policy engine refuses to auto-merge it and
labels it for human review. You keep visibility: you can see that 4.2.0 exists,
read the changelog, and decide. Nothing moves without a person.
mode: 'hard'
Renders an 'ignore' entry into dependabot.yml. NO PR IS EVER OPENED for the
ignored versions. Use only when the PR noise is genuinely unacceptable.
!! THE TRAP !!  An 'ignore' entry with a 'versions' range ALSO suppresses
SECURITY update PRs for those versions. You can silently sit on a known CVE and
never be told by a pull request. Two mitigations, both applied by this POC:
a) prefer 'ignoreUpdateTypes' (semver-scoped) over 'ignoreVersions' (range-scoped),
because semver-scoped ignores are far less likely to swallow a security fix;
b) Get-DependencyUpdateReport.ps1 reconciles every hard pin against the open
Dependabot alerts and raises PINNED-AND-VULNERABLE as a hard failure.
Dependabot ALERTS are never suppressed by dependabot.yml - only PRs are. The report
is therefore the backstop that makes hard pinning safe to use at all.
Every pin requires an owner and a reviewBy date. Pins without an expiry become
permanent by accident; the report flags expired ones.

entries.reason: Serialization behaviour differences across majors have broken API contracts for us before. Every bump gets a human and a contract-test run.
Npgsql 9 requires a server-side upgrade we have not scheduled. Holding until the database migration lands.
Tied to the .NET LTS major we currently target. Bumped deliberately as part of a framework upgrade, never piecemeal.
Angular majors require a coordinated ng update across the whole workspace.
TypeScript minors introduce new type errors in existing code. Always human-reviewed, never auto-merged.

tiers.description: Known vulnerability, CVSS >= 7.0. Fastest path to production.
Test/build-time only dependency. Blast radius is CI, not production.
Production dependency, patch bump. Semver says no API change.
Production dependency, minor bump. New surface area, backwards compatible in theory.
Breaking change by definition. Always a human decision.

denyAutoMerge.comment: Belt and braces. Anything matching these is forced to requiredHumanApprovals >= 1 regardless of tier, because a compromised or mis-scored package here is unrecoverable. Soft pins from the 'pins' section are merged into this list automatically at evaluation time - you do not need to repeat them here.

grouping.comment: Grouping collapses many small PRs into one, which cuts CI cost and review load. Never group security updates - they need to be independently revertible.
